options.label: One role at production depth (Rider)
options.description: Rider's 7 screens only, but genuinely finished: real camera, real geofence, real offline queue, real ledger call, Marathi default, all 7 states. Matches the Build Protocol's Phase 4 slice. Narrow, but everything after it is a copy.

questions.question: Which client platform? This one is hard to reverse.

options.label: Expo (React Native + Web) (Recommended)
options.description: One codebase, native builds for field roles and a web export for Customer/Sales/Admin/Owner. Only route that delivers background GPS and isFromMockProvider mock-location detection, which Law 11 requires to protect the payment model. Customer still gets a browser URL via the web export.

options.label: Web PWA only
options.description: Next.js or Vite + React, installable PWA, single deployment. Customer installs nothing, camera and foreground GPS work. Accepts that background location tracking and mock-location detection are not achievable — Immovable 3's anti-spoofing would be partially unenforced.

options.label: Split: Expo native for field, Next.js for desk
options.description: Expo native app for Rider/Technician/QC, separate Next.js web app for Customer/Sales/Admin/Owner. Each surface optimally built, but two codebases means the design system, i18n catalogues and API client are shared packages in a monorepo.

questions.question: Which map engine? Law 2 makes this the most-used component in the product.

options.label: MapLibre GL + MapTiler/PMTiles (Recommended)
options.description: Open source, no per-load metering, and self-hosted tiles make the 'pre-download the assigned area at job accept' requirement genuinely achievable. Costs you tile-pipeline setup (planetiler/tippecanoe + object storage).

options.label: Google Maps
options.description: Best Indian address, POI and Plus Code data — real accuracy gains for rider capture and customer site pins. Costs more at scale, free tier cut to ~28.5k loads in 2026, and offline tile pre-download is not supported the way this product needs.

options.label: Mapbox
options.description: Polished SDK, 50k free loads/month, good offline support in the native SDKs. Middle ground on cost, but proprietary licence and still metered per load.

questions.question: What backs the UI during this phase?

options.label: Mock fixtures behind a typed API contract (Recommended)
options.description: Define the full TypeScript API contract now (money in integer paise, server timestamps, settings keys, evidence rows), serve it from an in-repo mock. UI moves at full speed; swapping in the real backend later is a transport change, not a rewrite.

options.label: Real thin backend from day one
options.description: Stand up Postgres, migration 001 with tenant_id, the append-only ledger, the effective-dated settings store and the ID generator before UI work — the Build Protocol's Phase 3 walking skeleton. Slower to first beautiful screen, but the immovables are real rather than mocked.

Based on my search results, I found information about delivery rider partner apps in India from major platforms like Swiggy and Zomato. Here's what I discovered:

## Swiggy Delivery Partner App

The Swiggy app includes earnings and incentives information. Partners can earn up to ₹60,000 per month with joining bonus up to ₹10,000 and additional daily incentives. The app offers attractive incentives, bonuses, surge pay during high demand, and referral rewards.

To maintain constant sync with servers, the mobile application runs in background for longer duration (on average 4–5 hours each session) and involves data such as tracking location info of delivery partners (needed to assign trips, real-time tracking of an order, payment based on distance travelled).

## Zomato Delivery Partner App

| Slipping 1 day | 🤖 Diagnostic push: "Which is blocking you — material, site access, or a technical issue?" with three tappable answers |
| Slipping 2 days | 🚨 Admin notified; helper offered at company cost; on-time bonus at risk |

**Layer 3 — the honest reason the 2-week rule is enforceable here and nowhere else:**
In traditional elevator businesses, installations slip because *nobody can prove why*. Every party blames the other and there is no timestamped record. Here, every delay has an owner in the data: if the customer's shaft was wet, there is a photo; if the material arrived late, there is a container GPS log; if the technician was absent, there is a missing geofence check-in. **The deadline is enforceable because the blame is attributable.** That is the actual innovation — not the deadline itself.

**Filters (multi-select, instant):** role · zone · status · date range · value band · SLA breach only · alerts only · specific person · specific job ID.

**Lasso tool:** draw any shape on the map → everything inside it is filtered → export or bulk-action.

### **A2 — Alert Queue (the actual job)**

One prioritised list. The admin works top-down and stops when it is empty.

| Priority | Alert | Auto-action already taken |
|---|---|---|
| 🚨 **P0** | Safety incident / person trapped in lift | Emergency dispatch fired, admin phone ringing |
| 🚨 **P0** | Container tamper detected | Siren active, CCTV clip attached, police contact ready |
| 🔴 **P1** | AI evidence failed twice | Step frozen, technician notified, awaiting human call |

Every alert card carries: the ID, the map location, the full evidence, what the system already did, and **2–3 one-tap decisions**. The target is a median resolution time under 90 seconds.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about micro-interaction motion design trends for 2026, including reward animations, fintech applications, haptics, and spring physics:

## Key Trends in 2026

**Spring Physics Over Duration-Based Timing**

The new standard of motion design relies on Spring Physics, not duration-based timing. Leading companies are using advanced techniques like spring physics for more natural, less robotic movements. This approach creates more organic, life-like animations compared to traditional linear easing.

**Optimal Duration Guidelines**

Micro-interactions are meant to be light and fast, with an ideal duration between 200 and 500 milliseconds—long enough to be noticed, yet short enough to maintain flow. If important actions take 300 milliseconds to animate, this timing should be consistent across your interface.

**Haptic Feedback Integration**

Haptic feedback is becoming a crucial component of microinteractions on mobile and wearable devices, with subtle haptics when toggling, ticking checkboxes, or confirming payments making digital actions feel incredibly tangible and satisfying. As mobile devices increasingly support haptic feedback, designers are integrating subtle vibrations with visual micro-interactions, where a button click combining visual animation with light haptic feedback creates a richer, more immersive interaction.

**Fintech Applications**

Based on the search results, here's what the latest resources reveal about multi-brand design token architecture in 2026:

## Three-Tier Token Architecture

The three token layers are: Primitive (blue-500) feeds Semantic (action-color) feeds Component (button-bg-primary). The 3-tier model (Primitive → Semantic → Component) is the architectural standard for scalable token systems.

**The layers work as follows:**

- **Primitives**: Primitive tokens hold raw values with no opinion about usage — blue-500, space-4, radius-md.
- **Semantic**: Semantic tokens name intent rather than value — action-color points at blue-500, and a dark mode simply re-points it at a lighter blue.
- **Component**: Component tokens are the per-element specifics — button-bg-primary references action-color, never the primitive.

## Multi-Brand and Theming at Scale

The 3-tier model enables multi-brand setups: Primitive tokens remain identical across all brands. Semantic tokens are overridden per brand. The same principle scales to multi-brand scenarios. The semantic layer stays identical. Components stay identical. You ship one codebase with multiple token sets.

## Operational Benefits

Get the layering right and a single value change propagates cleanly across every surface. Change a raw value once and it cascades; rename a semantic role and components never notice the underlying primitive moved.

## Standards

The W3C Design Tokens Community Group shipped its first stable Design Tokens Format Module (v2025.10) on October 28, 2025, backed by 24+ organizations including Adobe, Google, Meta, and Figma.

1 # Imagine — Visual Creation Suite 2 3 ## Modules 4 Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: 5 - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams 6 - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards 7 - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls 8 - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) 9 - `art` — illustration and generative art 10 Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. 11 12 **Complexity budget — hard limits:** 13 - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. 14 - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. 15 - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. 16 17 If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. 18 19 **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) 20 21 You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. 22 23 ## Core Design System 24 25 These rules apply to ALL use cases. 26 27 ### Philosophy 28 - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. 29 - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. 30 - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. 31 - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. 32 33 ### Streaming 34 Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. 35 - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. 36 - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. 37 - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. 38 - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. 39 - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. 40 41 ### Rules 42 - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) 43 - No font-size below 11px 44 - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. 45 - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects 46 - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) 47 - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. 48 - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. 49 - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. 50 - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. 51 - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. 52 - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. 53 - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically. 54 - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. 55 - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. 56 - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. 57 - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. 58 - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. 59 - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). 60 - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) 61 - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. 62 - **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. "Enter an answer first") and stop — do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field. 63 - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global — never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag. 64 - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. 65 66 ### CSS Variables 67 **Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (card), `--surface-0` (page bg); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}` 68 **Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}` 69 **Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}` 70 **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono` 71 **Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px` 72 All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables. 73 74 **Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes: 75 - In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. 76 - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. 77 - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. 78 - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? 79 80 ### sendPrompt(text) 81 A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. 82 83 ### Links 84 `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. 85 86 ## When nothing fits 87 Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: 88 - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory 89 - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object 90 - All core design system rules still apply 91 - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking 92 93 94 ## UI components 95 96 ### Layout width 97 The widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns — auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width. 98 99 ### Aesthetic 100 Flat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai — like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else. 101 102 ### Tokens 103 - Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--border)` (or `--border-strong` for emphasis) 104 - Corner radius: `var(--radius)` for most elements, `12px` for cards 105 - Cards: white bg (`var(--surface-2)`), 0.5px border, 12px radius, padding 1rem 1.25rem 106 - Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled — write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width). 107 - Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px `--border-strong` border, hover `--surface-1`, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a ↗ arrow. 108 - **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts — `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context — integers for counts, 1–2 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step="1"` (or step="0.1" etc.) so the input itself emits round values. 109 - Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px) 110 - Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs 111 112 ### Metric cards 113 For summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) — surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--surface-1)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border). 114 115 ### Layout 116 - Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally 117 - Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing 118 - Don't put tables here — output them as markdown in your response text 119 120 **Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default — children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp. 121 122 **Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (≤700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper. 123 124 ### Mockup presentation 125 Contained mockups — mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components — should sit on a background surface (`var(--surface-1)` container with `border-radius: 12px` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper. 126 127 ### 1. Interactive explainer — learn how something works 128 *"Explain how compound interest works" / "Teach me about sorting algorithms"* 129 130 Use HTML for the interactive controls — sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. "Enter an answer first") and stop — do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global — never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? ### sendPrompt(text) A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. ### Links `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. ## When nothing fits Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object - All core design system rules still apply - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking ## UI components ### Layout width The widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns — auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width. ### Aesthetic Flat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai — like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else. ### Tokens - Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--border)` (or `--border-strong` for emphasis) - Corner radius: `var(--radius)` for most elements, `12px` for cards - Cards: white bg (`var(--surface-2)`), 0.5px border, 12px radius, padding 1rem 1.25rem - Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled — write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width). - Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px `--border-strong` border, hover `--surface-1`, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a ↗ arrow. - **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts — `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context — integers for counts, 1–2 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step="1"` (or step="0.1" etc.) so the input itself emits round values. - Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px) - Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs ### Metric cards For summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) — surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--surface-1)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border). ### Layout - Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally - Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing - Don't put tables here — output them as markdown in your response text **Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default — children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp. **Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (≤700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper. ### Mockup presentation Contained mockups — mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components — should sit on a background surface (`var(--surface-1)` container with `border-radius: 12px` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper. ### 1. Interactive explainer — learn how something works *"Explain how compound interest works" / "Teach me about sorting algorithms"* Use HTML for the interactive controls — sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Whitespace is the container. ```html <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;"> <label style="font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);">Years</label> <input type="range" min="1" max="40" value="20" id="years" style="flex: 1;" /> <span style="font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; min-width: 24px;" id="years-out">20</span> </div> <div style="display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;"> <span style="font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);">£1,000 →</span> <span style="font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500;" id="result">£3,870</span> </div> <div style="margin: 2rem 0; position: relative; height: 240px;"> <canvas id="chart"></canvas> </div> ``` Use `sendPrompt()` to let users ask follow-ups: `sendPrompt('What if I increase the rate to 10%?')`

Tokens are unprefixed CSS custom properties (`--text-primary`, `--surface-1`, `--border`) declared on `:root` by `@ant/cds/tokens.vanilla.css`, with dark-mode overrides under `[data-mode="dark"]` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. References below to `CdsRoot`, `Button`, or Tailwind utilities belong to the React build; in vanilla, read a utility like `bg-surface-1` as the underlying `var(--surface-1)`. ## Rules ### Token rule Reference purpose-layer tokens as CSS custom properties: ```css /* GOOD */ background: var(--surface-1); color: var(--text-secondary); border: 0.5px solid var(--border); /* BAD — raw hex, invisible in dark mode */ color: #3d3d3a; ``` | Property | Tokens | | ---------- | ------ | | Background | `--surface-{0..3,popover,panel}` · `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro,neutral}` · `--fill-{role}` | | Text | `--text-{primary,secondary,muted,disabled}` · `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro}` · `--on-{role}` | | Border | `--border` (default hairline) · `--border-{strong,stronger}` · `--border-{role}` | | Sizing | `--h-control` · `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}` · `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` · `--radius` | | Typography | `--font-{sans,mono,voice}` · `--font-size-{caption,footnote,body,prose,code,heading,title}` | | Shadow | `--shadow-{sm,md,lg,popover}` | | Motion | `--dur-{fast,snap,base,slow}` · `--ease-{out,snap,overshoot}` | ### Dark mode rule Dark mode is `[data-mode="dark"]` on `:root` (or `prefers-color-scheme: dark` with no explicit `data-mode`). All tokens flip automatically — never hardcode a dark-mode override. ### Muted text rule Supporting copy uses `color: var(--text-secondary)`; reserve `var(--text-muted)` for placeholders, captions, and metadata. **Never** `opacity` on text — opacity multiplies against the background and drifts per-surface. ### Accent rule At most **one** accent-filled (`variant="primary"`) Button per view; siblings use `secondary` or `ghost`. The `brand` (clay) role is reserved for Claude-initiated actions — send, generate — never ordinary user CTAs.

content.text:
Four more findings from the deeper search that directly shaped what you just saw:

**Icons are not universal, and this is measured.** ACM HCI research on low-literate smartphone users in India found abstract glyphs are *semantically opaque* — users consistently prefer concrete, photorealistic representations, and common navigation icons need "actionable contextualisation" to be understood ([ACM](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3449210), [UW/Medhi-Thies](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse490c/18au/readings/medhi-thies-2015.pdf)). Colour-coded interfaces plus voice annotation in the local language is the pattern that works. That's why the rider capture screen shows three photo thumbnails rather than three icons, and why status is carried by colour *and* shape, never colour alone.

**The Entity Card is a three-state bottom sheet.** Law 2's "tap any pin → card slides up" is the Google Maps peek/mid/full pattern, now the default container for anything that doesn't deserve a full-screen takeover. The hard part is nested scroll coordination and keeping the map interactive behind a non-modal sheet ([NN/g](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/bottom-sheet/), [Mobbin](https://mobbin.com/glossary/bottom-sheet)).

**Motion has moved off duration-based easing.** The 2026 standard is spring physics, 200–500ms, paired with haptics — and the fintech evidence is specific, e.g. a spring-loaded confirmation with a haptic tick cutting abandonment queries 9% ([micro-interactions 2026](https://bricxlabs.com/blogs/micro-interactions-2025-examples), [Primotech](https://primotech.com/ui-ux-evolution-2026-why-micro-interactions-and-motion-matter-more-than-ever/)). Law 4 demands under 3 seconds from effort to reward — spring + haptic + sound is that budget.

**Tokens now have a real standard.** The W3C Design Tokens Format Module hit stable v2025.10 in October 2025, backed by Adobe, Google, Meta and Figma ([token architecture 2026](https://timgraf.com/ui/design-token-architecture-2026-the-strategic-blueprint-for-scalable-design-systems/)). Worth building the five themes on it rather than a bespoke format.

One correction to my earlier note: the manual specifies 72px targets for the rider, which I'd flagged against a 48–56px research floor. Having read the gloved-precision numbers properly — thick gloves degrade effective touch precision to 20–25mm — 72px is not generous, it's correct for a helmeted rider, and 56px is the right number for the technician's gloved tick targets, not for the rider's primary action.

What holds all five themes together is a shared anatomy, identical everywhere: map underneath → three-state entity card → money meter in the top strip → task card with exactly four facts (work, distance, time, money) → draggable help bubble that knows the screen ID. Only density, contrast and control size change between roles.

# AIEC — UI foundation, first build phase

## Context

`C:\Users\allin\AIEC UI` is an empty directory — no git, no code. The product is
specified by two documents: `AIEC_App_Manual.md` (what it does, 2,068 lines) and
`AIEC_BUILD_PROTOCOL.md` (how it gets built, ten immovables + a phase machine).

The user's instruction was to research the best, most detailed UI first and see the
UI direction before any building starts. That research is done and the visual
direction has been rendered and reviewed in-conversation (five role themes, rider
Sunlight screens, technician Slate + customer Premium, admin Command, owner Executive).

**Deliberate deviation, on the record.** The Build Protocol's Part 14 sets build
order as compliance → payment → offline → evidence → features, and names "app first,
compliance later" as the fastest way to lose the business. Going UI-first inverts
that. It is workable — a UI built against a typed API contract forecloses nothing —
but this plan keeps money, evidence and gate logic as *server-authoritative contract
stubs* so none of it gets baked into components and has to be unpicked later.

## Research conclusions (settled)

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Component base | shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 | Five themes = five CSS-variable blocks, not five component forks. You own the source. |
| Polish layer | Untitled UI React patterns | Tailwind v4.2 + React Aria + TS 5.9, Figma-synced. Reference, not dependency. |
| Token format | W3C Design Tokens Format Module v2025.10 | Stable Oct 2025, backed by Adobe/Google/Meta/Figma. 3-tier: primitive → semantic → component. |
| Map | MapLibre GL + PMTiles | Only route where "pre-download the assigned area at job accept" actually works. No per-load metering. |
| Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari UI | Purpose-built for interfaces; tighter vertical metrics than the text cut, which matters at 72px buttons and in dense Admin tables. |
| Motion | Spring physics, 200–500ms, + haptics | 2026 standard. Law 4 needs effort→reward under 3s. |

Ergonomics, from research rather than taste: **72px** rider primary action (helmeted,
one-handed, in glare — not generous, correct); **56px** technician tick targets
(gloves degrade effective precision to 20–25mm); WCAG AA (4.5:1 / 3:1) as the floor,
not the sunlight target. Icons are semantically opaque to low-literate users — pair
every icon with colour, shape and voice; prefer photo thumbnails to glyphs.

## The UI direction

**Five themes, one anatomy.** Sunlight (rider), Slate (technician/QC), Premium
(customer), Command (admin), Executive (owner). Only density, contrast and control
size differ. Shared across all five, identical everywhere:

- Map underneath — no list-first screen exists anywhere (Law 2)
- Entity card as a three-state bottom sheet (peek / mid / full), non-modal, map stays live
- Money meter in the top strip
- Task card with exactly four facts: work, distance, time, money
- Draggable help bubble carrying `screen_id`

**Seven states per screen, all of them.** Loading, empty, error, partial,
permission-denied, offline (with queue depth visible), and blocked-by-gate. The
seventh names the gate, what unblocks it, and who can act — a gate that blocks
without explaining itself produces the phone call the product exists to remove.

## Build order for this phase

1. **Scaffold + token layer.** Repo init, Tailwind v4, W3C-format token pipeline
   emitting five theme blocks from one primitive set. Theme switch at the root.
2. **i18n from the first commit.** EN / मराठी / हिंदी catalogues, Indian numbering
   formatter (`₹1,50,000`) in the shared layer only. A missing key is a build break.
   Language switch must not lose form state.
3. **Shared anatomy components.** Map shell, three-state entity card, money meter,
   task card, help bubble, and the seven state components as first-class primitives.
4. **Role shells.** Nine navigation shells, correct theme and default language each.
5. **Flagship screens.** Rider R1/R2/R5, Technician T2, Customer C1, Admin A1+A2,
   Owner panels 1–4 — every one with all seven states.
6. **Typed API contract + mock.** Money in integer paise, server timestamps, settings
   keys, evidence rows. No arithmetic on money in any component.

## Open decisions

These were put to the user and dismissed; defaults below are what this plan assumes
unless redirected.

1. **Scope** — assume design system + all nine shells + flagship screens (~20 screens
   at production polish), remainder scaffolded with real routes and empty states.
2. **Platform** — assume **Expo (React Native + Web)**. This is the consequential one:
   a browser cannot check `isFromMockProvider`, so a PWA-only build leaves Law 11's
   mock-location detection structurally unenforceable, and that check protects the
   payment model. Expo's web export still gives the customer a browser URL with
   nothing to install.
3. **Map** — MapLibre GL + PMTiles as above.
4. **Data** — mock fixtures behind the typed contract.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `build` green; commands recorded in `docs/VERIFY.md`
- Every i18n key present in all three catalogues — missing key fails the build
- Grep gates: no `type="file"` / `ImagePicker` in any evidence path; no `Date.now()`
  in ledger/SLA/evidence paths; no numeric literal in a money or rate path
- Rendered and looked at: small viewport, in मराठी, with the network off
- All seven states seen rendered on every flagship screen, including blocked-by-gate
- Amounts render `₹1,50,000`, never `₹150,000`

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding NativeWind v4, Tailwind v4 support, and React Native tooling in 2026:

## Current Status

NativeWind v4 and v4.1 were updated in December 2025 to reflect the latest changes, including the new jsxImportSource transform, improved style merging through the updated StyleSheet, dark mode, support for CSS variables and custom CSS files, container queries, animations, and tvOS support.

## Tailwind v4 Migration Path

There's an active migration toward Tailwind CSS v4 in Expo with react-native-css and NativeWind v5 for universal styling. However, developers upgrading from NativeWind v4 to v5 have reported that many theme-based styles are not applied and light/dark mode does not work at all.

## Ecosystem Support

NativeWind is the foundation layer most shadcn-for-React-Native projects (including React Native Reusables and NativeCN) build on top of. React Native Reusables is described as universal shadcn/ui for React Native featuring a focused collection of components, crafted with NativeWind v4 and accessibility in mind.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding NativeWind v4, Tailwind v4 support, and React Native tooling in 2026:

## Current Status

NativeWind v4 and v4.1 were updated in December 2025 to reflect the latest changes, including the new jsxImportSource transform, improved style merging through the updated StyleSheet, dark mode, support for CSS variables and custom CSS files, container queries, animations, and tvOS support.

## Tailwind v4 Migration Path

There's an active migration toward Tailwind CSS v4 in Expo with react-native-css and NativeWind v5 for universal styling. However, developers upgrading from NativeWind v4 to v5 have reported that many theme-based styles are not applied and light/dark mode does not work at all.

## Ecosystem Support

NativeWind is the foundation layer most shadcn-for-React-Native projects (including React Native Reusables and NativeCN) build on top of. React Native Reusables is described as universal shadcn/ui for React Native featuring a focused collection of components, crafted with NativeWind v4 and accessibility in mind.

## Production-Ready Templates

Production-ready Expo + React Native + TypeScript starter kits are available with NativeWind for Tailwind styling, pre-styled UI components, dark mode support, and Expo Router for navigation.

The ecosystem is actively evolving, with NativeWind v4 being stable but v5 (with Tailwind v4 support) experiencing adoption challenges as of 2026.

content.text: Bundle runs now. New runtime error — something calls NativeWind's `colorScheme.set()` while dark mode is media-based. Our themes are explicit, so switching NativeWind to class-based dark mode is the right fix:

input.command:
cd "C:/Users/allin/AIEC UI" && python - <<'PY'
import io
p = "tailwind.config.js"
s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
old = '  content: ["./app/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],'
new = '''  content: ["./app/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
  // Explicit themes, not media queries: the role decides the palette, so the
  // dark/light flag must be settable rather than read from the OS.
  darkMode: "class",'''
assert old in s
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old, new))

# ALL INDIA ELEVATORS COMPANY — Platform
Pune pilot · Owner: Mr. Prashant Vasant Wable · One codebase, nine roles.

## Source of truth
- `C:\pppppppppp\PPPPPP PROMPTS\AIEC_App_Manual.md` — the product. Read by Part, never whole.
- `C:\pppppppppp\PPPPPP PROMPTS\AIEC_BUILD_PROTOCOL.md` — how it gets built. Read at phase gates.

## Stack (decided, verified running)
Expo SDK 57 · React Native 0.86 · React 19.2.3 · expo-router (file-based)
NativeWind v4.2.6 on **Tailwind v3.4** · react-native-svg · TypeScript 6

**Tailwind stays on v3.** NativeWind v5 (the Tailwind v4 route) has reported
breakage in theme-based styles and dark mode, which is precisely this project's
core mechanism — five themes over CSS variables. Do not "upgrade" it.

**expo-router is not compatible with react-navigation as of SDK 56.** Import
`ThemeProvider`, `DarkTheme`, `DefaultTheme`, `Theme` from `expo-router` itself.
Installing `@react-navigation/*` breaks the bundler with an explicit error.

## Build & verify
- Dev server: `npx expo start --web --port 8081`
- Typecheck: `npm run typecheck`
- i18n parity: `npm run i18n:check`
- Both: `npm run verify`
- Full list: `docs/VERIFY.md`. Run all of it before claiming anything.

## Architecture
- `src/design/` — three-tier tokens. `palette.ts` is tier 2 (semantic, per theme),
  applied via NativeWind `vars()` in `theme-provider.tsx`. Components use Tailwind
  class names only and never see a hex.
- `src/design/themes.ts` — per-theme sizing, role→theme and role→language maps.
- `src/i18n/` — catalogues typed against English, so a missing key fails `tsc`.
  `format.ts` owns Indian numbering; no component calls `Intl` directly.
- `src/components/states/` — all seven states in one file.
- `src/contract/` — typed API surface plus fixtures. Money is integer paise.
- `app/` — expo-router routes; one folder per role, each with its own layout.

## THE TEN IMMOVABLES
1. Nothing is done until something that is not you says so — evidence, always
2. Money is double-entry, append-only. No balance column, ever. Integer paise
3. Camera-only evidence. Server time only. Every rejection ships its appeal
4. No pink value in code. Settings store, effective-dated. No inline fallbacks
5. Multi-tenant from migration 001, enforced at the query layer
6. The person who does the work never approves it — query layer, not UI
7. Offline must work. No field path may await a network call
8. Every string externalised. EN / मराठी / हिंदी. ₹1,50,000 never ₹150,000
9. IDs generated centrally: MH-PUN-KOT-ORD-0041-K with Damm check
10. Demo and real never touch

## THE FIVE PAYMENT GATES (code, not reminders — no UI or admin override)
- No token → no agreement, no order
- No QC clearance → no drawings, no material
- No pre-dispatch payment → no supplier order placed
- No verified evidence → no technician payout accrual
- No final payment → no NOC

`src/contract/gates.ts` holds their *presentation* only. Enforcement is
server-side at the API; a gate that exists only in the UI is not a gate.

## Current state — read before assuming
The UI foundation exists and runs. There is **no backend**: screens render
fixtures from `src/contract/fixtures.ts`. Every money and evidence guarantee
the UI expresses is presentational until the server exists. The map is a
schematic SVG in `map-shell.tsx` with a MapLibre-shaped API, not MapLibre yet.

## Operating protocol
- YOU MUST NOT claim work complete without running `npm run verify` and pasting output.
- Every feature ships as a vertical slice with all seven states, including

- Look at the screen before calling it done: small viewport, in मराठी, network off.

content.text:
The server is running at **http://localhost:8081** and every route renders.

Three real bugs surfaced by actually running it, none of which typecheck would have caught:

1. **`babel-preset-expo` was never installed.** My `babel.config.js` referenced it, Metro failed to construct a transformer, and every bundle 500'd. It's in NativeWind's install list and I'd skipped it.
2. **React Navigation painted `rgb(242,242,242)` inside my theme wrapper**, washing out all three dark themes — the technician's step title was light-on-light and unreadable. Fixing it exposed a second fact: **expo-router is no longer compatible with react-navigation as of SDK 56**, so installing `@react-navigation/native` broke the bundler outright. The vendored `ThemeProvider`/`DarkTheme` come from `expo-router` itself.
3. **The language radios never reported their state.** Neither `accessibilityState.selected` nor `.checked` reaches `aria-checked` on web; it needs the `aria-checked` prop directly. A screen-reader user couldn't tell which language was active.

Also fixed along the way: the language switch clipped past the right edge on Sunlight (it was sized off the 56px control height, violating Law 9's 8px edge guard), Premium's serif bled onto button labels, and the owner's heatmap legend said "dark = expand here" while brighter cells were the high-opportunity ones.

**Verified, not asserted:** `npm run verify` green (typecheck + 126 i18n keys × 3 languages with placeholders aligned). Measured in the live DOM: capture button exactly **72px**, no horizontal overflow at 375px. Grep gates all zero — no gallery/file input in any evidence path, no `Date.now()` in money/evidence paths, no `balance` field, no raw hex outside the palette.

**Seen rendered:** rider in Marathi with offline queue depth, technician's gate card with its appeal route and "no override exists" line, customer's `₹5,53,500` in Indian grouping, admin's alert queue, owner's `MTD ₹1.42 Cr` from the compact formatter.

Two things I want to be plain about. The manual's language defaults work per role — rider and technician open in Marathi, customer in English — but **the fixture content itself is still English** ("Guide rail alignment", "Fishplate joint close-up"). Those are data, not UI strings, so they sit outside the catalogues; real content will come from the API. And **there is no backend** — the money and evidence guarantees these screens express are presentational. `src/contract/` is shaped so the transport swaps without touching components, and `CLAUDE.md` records this so a later session doesn't mistake the UI for enforcement.

The map is a schematic SVG with a MapLibre-shaped API (normalised 0..1 coordinates), not MapLibre itself — swapping it is a change inside `map-shell.tsx` only.

Next would be MapLibre + PMTiles behind that shell, or the remaining screens for the four scaffolded roles. Say which.

import io

# A hook so SVG strokes and raw style colours read the active palette.
p = "src/design/theme-provider.tsx"
s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
s = s.replace(
'''/** For components that genuinely need the role, not just its look. */''',
'''/**
 * Resolves a semantic token to a concrete `rgb(...)` string.
 *
 * Tailwind classes cover almost everything, but SVG strokes and a few raw
 * style props need a real colour value. This keeps those reading from the same
 * palette instead of hardcoding a hex that silently ignores the theme.
 */
export function useThemeColor(token: keyof SemanticTokens): string {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  return `rgb(${PALETTES[theme][token]})`;
}

/** For components that genuinely need the role, not just its look. */''')
s = s.replace(
'import { PALETTES } from "./palette";',
'import { PALETTES, type SemanticTokens } from "./palette";')
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
print("useThemeColor added")

s = s.replace(
'function ProgressRing({ percent }: { percent: number }) {\n  const radius = 42;',

s = s.replace('stroke="rgb(229 223 210)"', 'stroke={track}')
s = s.replace('stroke="rgb(154 107 30)"', 'stroke={fill}')
s = s.replace(
'import { useFormat, useT } from "@/i18n";',
'import { useThemeColor } from "@/design/theme-provider";\nimport { useFormat, useT } from "@/i18n";')

screen inventory for that role, layer 3 is the detail beneath each.

Ids are the manual's own (R3, T5, C7, Q2), so a support call or a bug report
can name an exact screen. The tree is held as data in
`src/navigation/screens.ts`, which is what the bottom navigation reads — so
routes and navigation cannot drift apart.

### Rider — Sunlight, मराठी default
| Layer | Screen | Route |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | R1 Ride map | `/rider` |
| 2 | R2 Capture confirm | `/rider/capture` |

| 2 | R7 Schedule | `/rider/schedule` |
| 3 | R7.1 Task detail with the escalation ladder | `/rider/schedule/[id]` |

### Technician — Slate, मराठी default

|---|---|---|

| 2 | T2 Today's SOP step | `/technician` |
| 2 | T3 Full SOP tree, 24 steps | `/technician/sop` |

| 2 | T5 Materials, phase-sealed kits | `/technician/materials` |
| 3 | T5.1 Kit detail | `/technician/materials/[kit]` |
| 2 | T6 Money meter | `/technician/money` |
| 3 | T6.1 Accrual with appeal route | `/technician/money/[id]` |
| 2 | T8 Training | `/technician/training` |
| 3 | T8.1 Module | `/technician/training/[id]` |

### Customer — Premium, English default, browser only
| Layer | Screen | Route |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | C1 My lift | `/customer` |
| 2 | C3 Shaft readiness | `/customer/shaft` |
| 3 | C3.1 Requirement detail | `/customer/shaft/[id]` |
| 2 | C5 Payments ladder | `/customer/payments` |
| 3 | C5.1 Receipt | `/customer/payments/[id]` |
| 2 | C6 Live container | `/customer/container` |
| 2 | C7 Installation progress | `/customer/progress` |
| 3 | C7.1 Day detail | `/customer/progress/[day]` |
| 2 | C8 Handover and NOC | `/customer/handover` |

### QC — Slate, मराठी default
| Layer | Screen | Route |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q1 Inspection map | `/qc` |
| 2 | Q2 Shaft clearance, 18 items | `/qc/clearance` |
| 3 | Q2.1 Check detail | `/qc/clearance/[item]` |

| 2 | Q5 Reports | `/qc/reports` |
| 3 | Q5.1 Report detail | `/qc/reports/[id]` |

`/` two doors · `/demo` role grid

## One layer only

`/admin` renders A1 live city map plus A2 alert queue as a single Command
screen. `/owner` renders all four Executive panels on one screen, which is
correct for that role — the manual is explicit that anything needing a second
layer does not belong on the owner view.

Neither has layer 2 or 3 yet.

## Not built — scaffold only

`/sales`, `/supplier`, `/onboarding` route and theme correctly but render a
coverage list rather than the screens themselves.

**Known defect:** those three scaffold lists carry English string literals
rather than catalogue keys, which breaks Immovable 8. They are placeholders,
not shipped screens, but the literals must go before any of them is built out.

## What layer 3 is for

Layer 3 is where Law 1 pays off. Each detail screen resolves one ID into its
complete record — the evidence, the timeline, the settings key that set the
amount, and the gate that is holding it. That is the forensic reconstruction
the payment model depends on: a dispute is settled by opening one screen, not
by assembling a case.

Three layers deep, built and running on **http://localhost:8081**. 44 screens, up from 12.

**Rider, technician, customer and QC** are now complete to layer 3 — the manual's screen inventory at layer 2, and the detail beneath each at layer 3. Full map in [docs/SCREENS.md](docs/SCREENS.md).

The layer-3 screens are where Law 1 actually pays off, and they're the reason this depth matters rather than just being more pages. The lead detail resolves one ID into its whole record — LEAD → EVID → WLET → CHAT → QUOT, each with its server timestamp. The wallet entry shows the settings key that set the amount (`lead.capture.credit`) next to the evidence that authorised it, so a worker can follow their own money back to the photograph. The locked SOP step shows the gate holding it rather than a dead button, and the accrual screen carries the appeal route on the same screen as the amount.

I held the tree as data in [src/navigation/screens.ts](src/navigation/screens.ts) rather than scattering it across route files, so the bottom navigation reads the same structure the routes use and the two can't drift.

**Four bugs found by looking at it, not by typechecking:**

- The tab bar clipped past the right edge — five tabs at Sunlight's 18px minimum text don't fit 375px. Rider dropped to four primaries and tab labels got capped at 12px. Then a second round: full screen titles truncated to "Shaft readi…" / "Live contai…", so tabs now carry short `tabLabelKey` forms. Measured after: 94px per tab, zero overflow, no truncation.
- Two screens had hardcoded `rgb(...)` literals that bypassed the palette — the grep gate only caught hex. Added a `useThemeColor` hook so SVG strokes and raw style props read the active theme, and the progress ring and trial-run chips now follow it.
- A route file was exporting fixture data, which expo-router treats specially. Moved to `fixtures-detail.ts`.
- Six sets of English literals slipped onto screens (escalation ladder, container sensors, QC verdicts, and a label built by interpolating an empty string into a sentence). All externalised — catalogues went 126 → 239 keys, all three languages aligned.

**Verified:** `npm run verify` green, 239 keys × 3 languages with placeholders matching. Grep gates all zero — no gallery input in evidence paths, no `Date.now()` in money paths, no `balance` field, no raw hex.

Two things to be straight about. **`/sales`, `/supplier` and `/onboarding` are still scaffolds**, and their coverage lists carry English literals — a real Immovable 8 break, recorded in SCREENS.md, harmless while they're placeholders but must go before they're built. And **`/admin` and `/owner` remain one layer** — for owner that's correct by design, since the manual says anything needing a second layer doesn't belong there; for admin it's simply not built yet.

Bash kept truncating on files past roughly 10KB regardless of quoting, so the larger screens went through the Write tool instead.

Next: admin's layer 2 and 3 (alert detail, approval desk, audit log), or the three scaffolded roles.
Continuing with admin — the manual calls it the most important section — then the three scaffolded roles. Reading the Parts I haven't yet:

content.text:
All nine roles are now built — **66 screens**, up from 44. Coverage in [docs/SCREENS.md](docs/SCREENS.md).

Added this round: **admin** three layers deep (alert queue → alert detail, approval desk → approval detail, money control, SOP/rate config → setting detail, audit log), **supplier** (order board → order detail, kit packing, container loading, fleet map, performance), **sales** (pipeline map, lead cards → pricing ladder, bot console, manual desk, quote builder), and **onboarding** (earnings calculator, quick check, details, training, first job). The three scaffolds are gone, which also closed the Immovable 8 break I flagged last turn.

Two screens are worth calling out because they make an immovable visible rather than just asserting it. **A7 config** is the settings store — every tunable number in the product, each with unit, range and effective date, which is the reason a numeric literal never needs to exist in code; A7.1 puts the effective date front and centre because "change a rate, reopen a closed job, its money must not move" is the property most likely to break silently. **S2.1** shows the 60/30/20 ladder as three stops, with no approve control at all below the margin floor — absent, not disabled.

**Two real spec mismatches I'd introduced earlier and have now corrected.** The manual gives sales and supplier a *light* Command variant — both work at a desk, not in a darkened control room — and I had them on admin's dark palette. And it puts onboarding on *Sunlight (aspirational)*, a job-seeker on a cheap phone outdoors, where I had Premium. So there are now six palettes, not five. Verified in the DOM: supplier resolves `rgb(255,255,255)` with blue primary, onboarding resolves the Sunlight orange with Marathi default.

Also fixed: English literals that crept into the new screens (KYC step names, supplier order states), a dead style object, and `RoleScaffold` — now unused — deleted.

**Verified:** `npm run verify` green, 337 keys × 3 languages aligned. All five grep gates zero, including the `rgb()` check I added last turn. Then walked **41 routes** programmatically: zero blank, zero horizontal overflow, zero truncated tab labels.

One honest note on method: screenshots came back mis-scaled partway through — the DOM reported a correct 375×812 while the capture showed content in a third of the frame. That's the capture pipeline while the browser pane is hidden, not a layout bug, so I switched to DOM assertions for the rest, which is why the verification above is measurements rather than pictures.

Still missing, listed in SCREENS.md: A3 role monitors, A6 analytics, A8 users, S6 conversion analytics, P5 supplier payments, C2 agreement, C4 drawings, C9 support bot, T4 evidence camera, T7 leaderboard, T9 escalate, Q3 post-install audit. And R2 is still a confirm screen rather than a live camera flow — that one needs real camera work, not more UI.

Everything remains fixtures. No backend, no MapLibre.

## OpenFreeMap and Free Vector Tile Options

OpenFreeMap has demonstrated that it's possible to offer free, production-ready map tiles without API keys or usage limits, while VersaTiles also provides open-source tools and infrastructure for serving free vector tiles.

OpenFreeMap's goal is to provide free, production-quality vector-tile hosting using existing tools including OpenStreetMap, OpenMapTiles, Planetiler, MapLibre, Natural Earth and Wikidata.

## Key Features

OpenFreeMap offers a fully free public instance with no API key, registration, cookies, or limits on map views and requests, supported by donations and featuring light styles such as Positron Bright Liberty 3D for clean, non-obtrusive basemaps; users can also self-host the open-source setup.

## Alternatives in the Ecosystem

Free, OpenStreetMap-based vector basemap alternatives include OpenMapTiles, Protomaps, OpenFreeMap and VersaTiles. Additionally, Maptoolkit.org is the latest project to join this growing ecosystem, offering a free, production-ready vector map service that requires no API keys, no user accounts and no request limits for qualifying users.

## MapLibre Compatibility

If you are using MapLibre, attributions are automatically added. This makes these tools particularly suitable for MapLibre-based projects.
